answer: The U.S. unemployment rate was 4.2% (seasonally adjusted) in September 2026, up from 4.1% in August. Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, via FRED series UNRATE (updated 2026-10-02).

Headline CPI inflation (CPI-U, all items, seasonally adjusted) was 3.4% year over year in August 2026 (3.35%), up from 3.30% in July. Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, via FRED series CPIAUCSL with the percent-change-from-year-ago transformation.

Total nonfarm payrolls rose by 29,000 jobs (seasonally adjusted) in September 2026, according to the report released 2026-10-02. August's change now stands at +133,000. Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, via FRED series PAYEMS (month-over-month change).

The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 7.28% for the week ending Thursday 2026-10-01, up from 7.03% the week before. Source: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey, via FRED series MORTGAGE30US.
The 10-year Treasury constant-maturity yield was 5.28% on 2026-10-02 (Friday), the latest daily value. Source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (H.15), via FRED series DGS10.

The effective federal funds rate averaged 3.75% in September 2026, up from 3.63% in August. Source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System / Federal Reserve Bank of New York, via FRED series FEDFUNDS.

Real GDP grew at a 2.2% seasonally adjusted annual rate in Q2 2026 (April-June), as of BEA's estimate published by FRED on 2026-09-30. Q1 2026 grew 2.5%. Source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, via FRED series A191RL1Q225SBEA.
Housing starts were 1,275,000 units at a seasonally adjusted annual rate in August 2026, down from 1,309,000 in July. Source: U.S. Census Bureau and HUD, via FRED series HOUST.

Initial jobless claims were 197,000 (seasonally adjusted) for the week ending Saturday 2026-09-26, down from 198,000 the week before. Source: U.S. Employment and Training Administration (Department of Labor), via FRED series ICSA.

The latest University of Michigan consumer sentiment reading on FRED is 51.7 (index, 1966:Q1=100) for August 2026, down from 55.2 in July. FRED's copy runs about a month behind the University of Michigan's own releases, so a September 2026 reading may already be out from the university, but it is not in FRED yet. Source: University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers, via FRED series UMCSENT.
In April 2020 the U.S. unemployment rate was 14.8% (seasonally adjusted). Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, FRED series UNRATE.
In October 2009 the U.S. unemployment rate was 10.0% (seasonally adjusted). Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, FRED series UNRATE.
The highest weekly 30-year fixed mortgage rate in 1981 was 18.63%, in the week ending October 9, 1981. Source: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey, FRED series MORTGAGE30US.
On March 9, 2020 the 10-year Treasury yield was 0.54% (constant maturity, daily). Source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, FRED series DGS10.

In June 2022 headline CPI inflation was about 9.0% year over year (8.98%, calculated from the seasonally adjusted CPI-U index). Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, FRED series CPIAUCSL (percent change from a year earlier).
In January 2006 housing starts ran at 2,273,000 units (2,273 thousand), seasonally adjusted annual rate. Source: U.S. Census Bureau and HUD, FRED series HOUST.

The lowest monthly reading of the University of Michigan consumer sentiment index in 2022 was 50.0 (index, 1966:Q1=100), in June 2022. Source: University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers, FRED series UMCSENT.
On April 20, 2020 the WTI crude oil spot price (Cushing, Oklahoma) was -$36.98 per barrel. Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, FRED series DCOILWTICO.
In April 2020 the U.S. personal saving rate was 31.8% (seasonally adjusted annual rate). Source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, FRED series PSAVERT.

In Q2 2020 U.S. real GDP fell at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 28.0% (-28.0%, change from the previous quarter), according to the current vintage. Source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, FRED series A191RL1Q225SBEA.
The effective federal funds rate averaged 19.04% in July 1981 (monthly average). Source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, H.15 release, via FRED series FEDFUNDS.
The median sales price of new houses sold in the U.S. was $442,600 in Q4 2022 (not seasonally adjusted). Source: U.S. Census Bureau and HUD, via FRED series MSPUS. This series covers new houses only.

The U.S. unemployment rate averaged about 3.7% over the 12 months of 2019 (seasonally adjusted). The exact mean of the monthly values is 3.675%, with a range of 3.5% to 4.0%. Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, via FRED series UNRATE.

Year-over-year headline CPI inflation was above 4% in 5 months of 2023: January (6.33%), February (5.96%), March (4.92%), April (4.95%) and May (4.13%). It fell to 3.07% in June and stayed below 4% for the rest of the year. Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, CPI-U all items, seasonally adjusted, via FRED series CPIAUCSL as percent change from a year earlier.
The highest weekly 30-year fixed mortgage rate in 2023 was 7.79%, in the week ending Thursday, October 26, 2023. Source: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey, via FRED series MORTGAGE30US.

The U.S. added about 1,459,000 nonfarm payroll jobs from December 2023 to December 2024. Total nonfarm employment rose from 156,857 thousand to 158,316 thousand (seasonally adjusted, current vintage as of October 2026). Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Employment Statistics, via FRED series PAYEMS.

The index rose about 129.6% from January 2012 to June 2022, from 134.157 to 308.055 (Jan 2000 = 100, not seasonally adjusted). Source: S&P Cotality Case-Shiller U.S. National Home Price Index, via FRED series CSUSHPINSA.

The most negative daily 10-year minus 2-year Treasury spread in 2023 was -1.08 percentage points, on July 3, 2023. The next lowest was -1.07 on March 8, 2023. Source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, via FRED series T10Y2Y.

3 quarters from 2020 through 2024 had negative annualized real GDP growth: 2020 Q1 (-5.2%), 2020 Q2 (-28.0%) and 2022 Q1 (-1.0%). In current revised data, 2022 Q2 is +0.6%, not negative. Source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, via FRED series A191RL1Q225SBEA (percent change at a seasonally adjusted annual rate).

The peak weekly number of initial jobless claims in 2020 was 6,137,000 (seasonally adjusted), for the week ending April 4, 2020. The week ending March 28, 2020 was close behind at 5,946,000. Source: U.S. Employment and Training Administration (Department of Labor), via FRED series ICSA.

The FRED tools here only return today's vintage, so I can't get the first print from FRED. From memory, and not from FRED: BLS first reported about +228,000 jobs for March 2025. The current data (BLS, PAYEMS as of 2026-10-06) shows +67,000 for March 2025 (change in total nonfarm payrolls, seasonally adjusted).

The first print isn't available through these FRED tools. From memory, and not from FRED: BLS first reported about +139,000 jobs for May 2025. The current data (BLS, PAYEMS as of 2026-10-06) shows +13,000 for May 2025 (seasonally adjusted).

The first print isn't available through these FRED tools. From memory, and not from FRED: BLS first reported about +147,000 jobs for June 2025. The current data (BLS, PAYEMS as of 2026-10-06) shows -20,000 for June 2025, a net loss (seasonally adjusted).

The first print isn't available through these FRED tools. From memory, and not from FRED: BLS first reported about +73,000 jobs for July 2025. The current data (BLS, PAYEMS as of 2026-10-06) shows +64,000 for July 2025 (seasonally adjusted).

The advance estimate isn't available through these FRED tools. From memory, and not from FRED: BEA's advance estimate for Q1 2022 was -1.4% (annualized). The current data (BEA, A191RL1Q225SBEA, last updated 2026-09-30) shows -1.0% at a seasonally adjusted annual rate for 2022 Q1.

The advance estimate isn't available through these FRED tools. From memory, and not from FRED: BEA's advance estimate for Q2 2022 was -0.9% (annualized). The current data (BEA, A191RL1Q225SBEA, last updated 2026-09-30) shows +0.6% at a seasonally adjusted annual rate for 2022 Q2.

The advance estimate isn't available through these FRED tools. From memory, and not from FRED: BEA's advance estimate for Q4 2024 was 2.3% (annualized). The current data (BEA, A191RL1Q225SBEA, last updated 2026-09-30) shows 2.4% at a seasonally adjusted annual rate for 2024 Q4.

The latest data published by March 1, 2025 was the January 2025 unemployment rate, 4.0% (seasonally adjusted, BLS, released February 7, 2025). The release timing and that first-print figure are from memory, because these tools have no as-of-date option. Today's FRED UNRATE also shows 4.0% for January 2025.

These FRED tools can't return data as it stood on 2025-02-01. From memory, and not from FRED: the January 10, 2025 BLS release put December 2024 total nonfarm employment at about 159.2 million (roughly 159,222 thousand, seasonally adjusted). The current FRED PAYEMS value for December 2024, after the benchmark revisions, is 158,316 thousand (about 158.3 million).

The first print isn't available through these FRED tools. From memory, and not from FRED: when first reported in January 2025, year-over-year CPI inflation for December 2024 was about 2.9%. The current data (BLS CPI-U, seasonally adjusted, CPIAUCSL, percent change from a year earlier) shows 2.87% (about 2.9%) for December 2024.

Freddie Mac is the original source. It publishes the rate weekly, as of each Thursday, through its Primary Mortgage Market Survey. The series is in percent, not seasonally adjusted, and runs from 1971-04-02 to 2026-10-01 (latest observation). Since November 17, 2022, Freddie Mac has based the survey on applications lenders submit to it. Source: Freddie Mac via FRED series MORTGAGE30US.

The source is S&P Dow Jones Indices LLC. FRED's copy holds only 10 years of daily closing values, because of its licensing agreement with S&P DJI. As of 2026-10-06 it runs from 2016-10-06 to 2026-10-05. It is a price index, so dividends are not included, and it is not seasonally adjusted. Source: S&P Dow Jones Indices LLC via FRED series SP500.

The source is S&P Dow Jones Indices LLC. FRED's title is now 'S&P Cotality Case-Shiller U.S. National Home Price Index' (Cotality was formerly CoreLogic). It is monthly, with units of Index Jan 2000=100 and no seasonal adjustment, and runs from January 1987 to July 2026. Source: S&P Dow Jones Indices LLC via FRED series CSUSHPINSA.

It comes from the University of Michigan's Surveys of Consumers. The series is monthly, with units of Index 1966:Q1=100 and no seasonal adjustment. At the source's request FRED shows it one month late, so the latest observation is August 2026. Data before January 1978 are in series UMCSENT1. Source: University of Michigan via FRED series UMCSENT.

The source is the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), in its Spot Prices release. The series is the daily WTI spot price at Cushing, Oklahoma, in dollars per barrel and not seasonally adjusted. It runs from 1986-01-02 to 2026-09-29. Source: U.S. EIA via FRED series DCOILWTICO.

The source is the U.S. Department of Labor's Employment and Training Administration, in its Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims Report. Yes, the headline series is seasonally adjusted. It is weekly, for weeks ending Saturday, measured as a number of claims, and runs from 1967 to the week ending 2026-09-26. Source: U.S. Employment and Training Administration via FRED series ICSA.

Real GDP on FRED is in billions of chained 2017 dollars, at a seasonally adjusted annual rate. The series is quarterly and runs from Q1 1947 to Q2 2026. Source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis via FRED series GDPC1.

The units are an index with base period 1982-1984=100. The headline series is seasonally adjusted and monthly, running from January 1947 to August 2026. Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics via FRED series CPIAUCSL.

The U.S. Census Bureau and the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development publish it jointly, in the New Residential Sales release. FRED's metadata titles the series 'Median Sales Price of New Houses Sold for the United States'. It is quarterly, in dollars and not seasonally adjusted, and runs from Q1 1963 to Q2 2026. Source: U.S. Census Bureau and HUD via FRED series MSPUS.

The Federal Reserve Bank of New York is the source of the daily Effective Federal Funds Rate. It is a volume-weighted median of overnight federal funds trades reported on the FR 2420 report. The series is in percent and not seasonally adjusted, and runs from 2000-07-03 to 2026-10-02. Source: Federal Reserve Bank of New York via FRED series EFFR. I could not check the source of the monthly FEDFUNDS or daily DFF series, because the connector intermittently returned HTTP 403. My understanding, not from FRED, is that those two are credited to the Federal Reserve Board of Governors.
